ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: Seeing the Extraordinary in the Ordinary

fullPassage:
Creativity. When you hear this word, what instantly pops into your mind? You may think it is a quality that only artists and writers possess — some special talent you are either born with or without. Many people accept the idea that we can be divided into two groups: those who are creative and those who are not. This common belief, however, is far from the truth. Everyone has the ability to be creative. Finding creativity inside yourself just takes a little effort. Some artists, for example, spark their creativity by looking closely at ordinary objects. They try to discover the beauty hidden within these common objects and then turn them into works of art.

Look at these two paintings. Believe it or not, they both depict the same person, Holy Roman Emperor Rudolf II. The one on the left might look familiar, as it is a standard style of portrait that you would see in a gallery or an art book. However, the one on the right, called Vertumnus, is very unconventional. Created by a 16th-century Italian painter named Giuseppe Arcimboldo, the painting shows striking creativity and originality. Fruits, flowers, and vegetables are arranged like the pieces of a puzzle to create a human head. A cherry and a mulberry become the dark eyes, while an apple and a peach act as the pink cheeks. This painting is representative of the artist's signature style of "composite portraits." He used plants, animals, and other objects to create many other portraits like this.

Another good example of Arcimboldo's unique creativity can be found in The Gardener, one of his "reversible" paintings. When viewed normally, it is just an ordinary still life of vegetables in a bowl. However, when flipped upside down, it is magically transformed into a smiling face! Experts have studied this painting, along with Arcimboldo's other reversible ones. Their research showed that he first painted them as still life paintings and then turned them upside down and made some adjustments to create faces. X-ray examination revealed that he sometimes changed the positions of some of the fruits and vegetables. Why did he make his paintings reversible? It was probably because he wanted to add an interactive element to his work by doing so. Viewers feel as if they are playing a visual game, which brings them a sense of pleasure.

Each of Arcimboldo's works is a careful study of everyday objects. When he looked at typical objects, such as a bowl of vegetables, he saw the artistic and imaginative potential in them. His innovative approach to art inspired many great artists who came after him, including Pablo Picasso, Salvador Dalí, and René Magritte.

Take a look at this picture. Do you see a horse standing in a field? Or is it simply a collection of clothes hanging on a clothesline? This witty and amusing creation is actually a work of art created by the visual artist Helga Stentzel. Using everyday items, she creates playful visual illusions that force you to look twice in order to confirm what you have just seen. Her unique style has been called "household surrealism."

Stentzel is perhaps best known for her Clothesline Animals series. She got inspiration for the series while she was hanging her laundry. By simply adding some colorful clothespins and a dish towel, she was able to transform her black sweatshirt and dark grey pants into a horse. Other creations followed, including a brown cow standing on some hills and a zebra crossing the desert. All of these works were created from nothing more than laundry and household items.

Another series that highlights Stentzel's astonishing creativity is Edible Creatures. For this series, she arranges food items you can find in any kitchen to create cute animals. The stars of the series are Brad Pet and Crunchie, a pair of puppies made of sliced bread and lettuce respectively. Stentzel says she came up with the concept of Crunchie while putting together a salad for her family.

What do you think her secret is? Stentzel says that it is her active observation skills that allow her to make magic out of the ordinary. As a child, she would spend time staring at the patterns in the wood of her bed, trying to find different animal shapes. She admits that even today she stares at things longer than is acceptable in society. This keen observation is what enables her to continuously produce creative and imaginative works of art.

Creativity is not some kind of exceptional skill that belongs to exclusive groups of people. It is actually a part of our daily lives, a power that we can display anytime we choose to. Whether we realize it or not, we are constantly using our creativity to adapt, adjust, and rearrange the things around us. By doing so, we are turning the ordinary into something extraordinary — something that has never been seen before. Take a look at the things around you, but don't just give them a quick glance. Look carefully, and you might discover something that sparks your own imagination and creativity.

questions.passage: You may think it is a quality that only artists and writers possess. Many people accept the idea that we can be ①<u>divided</u> into two groups: those who are creative and those who are not. This common belief, however, is far from the truth. Everyone has the ability to ②<u>be</u> creative. Finding creativity inside yourself just ③<u>takes</u> a little effort. Some artists spark their creativity by ④<u>look</u> closely at ordinary objects.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'by looking'인데, 'look'으로 바뀌어 틀림. 전치사 by 뒤에 동명사 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① divided: can be divided 수동태 정상
✅ ② be: ability to be 정상
✅ ③ takes: Finding(동명사 주어, 단수) + takes 정상
❌ ④ look → looking: by(전치사) + 동명사
det.tip: by + ~ing: ~함으로써. 전치사 뒤 동사원형 불가.

questions.passage: Created by a 16th-century Italian painter named Giuseppe Arcimboldo, the painting shows striking creativity and originality. Fruits, flowers, and vegetables are ①<u>arranged</u> like the pieces of a puzzle to create a human head. A cherry and a mulberry become the dark eyes, while an apple and a peach ②<u>act</u> as the pink cheeks. This painting is ③<u>representative</u> of the artist's signature style. He used plants, animals, and other objects ④<u>create</u> many other portraits like this.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'to create'인데, to가 빠져서 틀림. 목적의 to부정사.
det.analysis:
✅ ① arranged: are arranged 수동태 정상
✅ ② act: 복수주어(an apple and a peach) + act 정상
✅ ③ representative: is representative of ~ 정상
❌ ④ create → to create: 목적의 to부정사 필요
det.tip: 목적의 to부정사: He used objects to create = 만들기 위해 사용했다.

questions.passage: Stentzel says that it is her active observation skills ①<u>that</u> allow her to make magic out of the ordinary. As a child, she would spend time ②<u>staring</u> at the patterns in the wood of her bed, trying to find different animal shapes. She admits that even today she stares at things ③<u>longer</u> than is acceptable in society. This keen observation is ④<u>that</u> enables her to continuously produce creative works.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'what enables her'인데, 'that'으로 바뀌어 틀림. '~하는 것'이라는 의미로 선행사 포함 관계대명사 what 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① that: 'It is ~ that …' 강조구문의 that 정상
✅ ② staring: spend time + ~ing 정상
✅ ③ longer: 비교급 정상
❌ ④ that → what: 'This keen observation is what enables her' — what = the thing that(~하는 것)
det.tip: what vs that: what = 선행사 포함(~하는 것). ①의 that은 강조구문, ④는 관계대명사 자리. 'is what enables' = ~를 가능하게 하는 것이다.

questions.passage: When viewed normally, it is just an ordinary still life of vegetables in a bowl. However, when flipped upside down, it is magically ①<u>transformed</u> into a smiling face! Experts have studied this painting, along with Arcimboldo's other reversible ones. Their research showed that he first painted them as still life paintings and then turned them upside down and made some ②<u>adjustments</u> to create faces. It was probably because he wanted to add an ③<u>interactive</u> element to his work. Viewers feel as if they are playing a visual game, which brings them a sense of ④<u>discomfort</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'pleasure(즐거움)'인데, 'discomfort(불편함)'로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① transformed(변환된): 원문 일치
✅ ② adjustments(수정): 원문 일치
✅ ③ interactive(상호작용적): 원문 일치
❌ ④ discomfort(불편함) → pleasure(즐거움): 게임하는 즐거움이므로 불편함은 부적절
det.tip: pleasure(즐거움) ↔ discomfort(불편함). 'playing a visual game' = 즐거운 경험.

questions.passage: Stentzel is perhaps best known for her Clothesline Animals series. She got ①<u>inspiration</u> for the series while she was hanging her laundry. By simply adding some colorful clothespins and a dish towel, she was able to transform her black sweatshirt and dark grey pants into a horse. Another series that highlights Stentzel's ②<u>astonishing</u> creativity is Edible Creatures. The stars of the series are Brad Pet and Crunchie, a pair of puppies made of sliced bread and lettuce ③<u>respectively</u>. Stentzel says she came up with the concept of Crunchie while ④<u>discarding</u> a salad for her family.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'putting together(만들다)'인데, 'discarding(버리다)'로 바뀌었다. 샐러드를 '만들다가' 아이디어를 떠올렸다는 문맥.
det.analysis:
✅ ① inspiration(영감): 원문 일치
✅ ② astonishing(놀라운): 원문 일치
✅ ③ respectively(각각): 원문 일치
❌ ④ discarding(버리다) → putting together(만들다): 샐러드를 '버리면서' 아이디어를 떠올렸다는 것은 비논리적
det.tip: putting together(만들다/조립하다) ↔ discarding(버리다). 'came up with the concept while ~'이 단서.

questions.passage: You may think it is a quality that only artists and writers possess — some special talent you are either born with or without. Many people accept the idea that we can be divided into two groups. This common belief, however, is far from the truth. Everyone has the ability to be creative. Finding creativity inside yourself just takes __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 내면의 창의력을 발견하는 것은 약간의 노력(a little effort)이 필요할 뿐이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① a little effort: 원문 일치. 특별한 재능이 아니라 약간의 노력이면 충분
❌ ② extraordinary talent: '타고나는 특별한 재능'이라는 통념을 반박하는 글
❌ ③ years of training: 원문에 근거 없음
❌ ④ professional guidance: 원문에 근거 없음
det.tip: 'just takes' = ~이면 충분하다. '타고난 재능 vs 누구나 가능' 대비가 핵심.

questions.passage: Each of Arcimboldo's works is a careful study of everyday objects. When he looked at typical objects, such as a bowl of vegetables, he saw the artistic and imaginative potential in them. His innovative approach to art inspired many great artists who came after him, including Pablo Picasso, Salvador Dalí, and René Magritte. Stentzel says that it is her active observation skills that allow her to __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: make magic out of the ordinary
avoid looking at things for too long

det.korean: 평범함 속에서 마법을 만든다(make magic out of the ordinary).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ make magic out of the ordinary: 원문 일치. 관찰력으로 평범한 것에서 마법을 만듦
❌ ① 다른 예술가 스타일을 따라하는 것이 아님
❌ ② 일상 사물을 무시하는 것이 아니라 관찰함
❌ ④ 오래 보는 것을 피하는 것이 아니라 오래 봄
det.tip: 'make magic out of the ordinary' = 평범함 속에서 마법을 만들다. active observation skills가 핵심.

questions.passage: Look at these two paintings. Believe it or not, they both depict the same person, Holy Roman Emperor Rudolf II. The one on the left might look familiar, as it is a standard style of portrait. However, the one on the right, called Vertumnus, is very unconventional. Created by a 16th-century Italian painter named Giuseppe Arcimboldo, the painting shows striking creativity and originality.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 두 그림은 서로 다른 인물을 묘사한다.

det.korean: ② 원문: 'a 16th-century Italian painter named Giuseppe Arcimboldo'와 일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ① '같은 인물(the same person)'
✅ ② '16세기 이탈리아 화가'와 일치
❌ ③ Vertumnus는 '매우 색다른(unconventional)' 것
❌ ④ 오른쪽 그림이 색다름
det.tip: 두 그림 = 같은 인물(Rudolf II). 왼쪽=전통적, 오른쪽(Vertumnus)=색다른.

questions.passage: Stentzel is perhaps best known for her Clothesline Animals series. She got inspiration for the series while she was hanging her laundry. By simply adding some colorful clothespins and a dish towel, she was able to transform her black sweatshirt and dark grey pants into a horse. Other creations followed, including a brown cow standing on some hills and a zebra crossing the desert.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Stentzel은 새로운 옷을 구매하여 작품을 만들었다.

det.korean: ④ 원문: 'She got inspiration while she was hanging her laundry'와 일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 동물원이 아니라 '빨래를 널다가'
❌ ② 새 옷이 아니라 기존 빨래와 가정용품
❌ ③ 첫 작품은 말(horse)
✅ ④ '빨래를 널다가 영감'과 일치
det.tip: hanging her laundry = 빨래를 널다. 첫 작품: sweatshirt+pants → horse.

questions.passage: Another series that highlights Stentzel's astonishing creativity is Edible Creatures. For this series, she arranges food items you can find in any kitchen to create cute animals. The stars of the series are Brad Pet and Crunchie, a pair of puppies made of sliced bread and lettuce respectively. Stentzel says she came up with the concept of Crunchie while putting together a salad for her family.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Edible Creatures 시리즈는 옷으로 동물을 만든다.

det.korean: ② 원문: 'came up with the concept of Crunchie while putting together a salad'와 일치.
det.analysis:
❌ ① Brad Pet은 '자른 빵(sliced bread)'으로 만듦. 양상추는 Crunchie
✅ ② '샐러드를 만들다가 Crunchie 아이디어'와 일치
❌ ③ 옷이 아니라 음식으로 동물을 만듦(Edible Creatures)
❌ ④ '어느 주방에서든 찾을 수 있는 식재료(food items you can find in any kitchen)'
det.tip: Brad Pet=빵, Crunchie=양상추. Clothesline=옷, Edible Creatures=음식. 시리즈 구분 주의.

questions.passage: Creativity is not some kind of exceptional skill that belongs to exclusive groups of people. It is actually a part of our daily lives, a power that we can display anytime we choose to. By doing so, we are turning the ordinary into something extraordinary — something that has never been seen before.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 창의력은 누구나 가지고 있으며 일상에서 발휘할 수 있다.
미술 교육의 중요성과 체계적인 훈련 방법
유명 화가들의 생애와 대표 작품 분석
현대 미술 시장의 경제적 가치와 투자 전략

det.korean: 주제: 창의력은 누구나 가지고 있으며 일상에서 발휘할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 'not exceptional skill' + 'part of our daily lives' + 'anytime we choose to'
❌ ② 미술 교육은 주제가 아님
❌ ③ 생애 분석이 아니라 창의성 메시지
❌ ④ 경제적 가치 언급 없음
det.tip: 'not exceptional' + 'part of our daily lives' + 'anytime' = 누구나 가진 일상의 힘.

questions.passage: Each of Arcimboldo's works is a careful study of everyday objects. When he looked at typical objects, such as a bowl of vegetables, he saw the artistic and imaginative potential in them. His innovative approach to art inspired many great artists who came after him. Stentzel says that it is her active observation skills that allow her to make magic out of the ordinary.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 Arcimboldo와 Stentzel의 공통점으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 둘 다 전통적인 화풍을 그대로 따른다.
둘 다 평범한 사물에서 창의적 가능성을 발견한다.

det.korean: 공통점: 평범한 사물에서 창의적 가능성을 발견한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ Arcimboldo: 채소에서 예술적 잠재력. Stentzel: 일상에서 마법. 둘 다 ordinary에서 extraordinary
❌ ① Stentzel은 현대 작가
❌ ② Arcimboldo는 과일/채소, Stentzel은 옷/음식 다양
❌ ③ 둘 다 unconventional/비전통적
det.tip: 'everyday objects' + 'ordinary' → extraordinary = 두 예술가의 공통 핵심.

questions.passage: Why did he make his paintings reversible? It was probably because he wanted to add an <u>interactive element</u> to his work by doing so. Viewers feel as if they are playing a visual game, which brings them a sense of pleasure. Each of Arcimboldo's works is a careful study of everyday objects.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 interactive element가 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 관객이 직접 그림을 그릴 수 있는 참여 기회
그림을 디지털로 변환하여 온라인에서 감상하는 기능
관객이 그림을 뒤집어 보며 시각적 재미를 느끼는 요소
전문가만 이해할 수 있는 숨겨진 기술적 장치

det.korean: interactive element = 관객이 그림을 뒤집어 보며 시각적 재미를 느끼는 요소
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 'Viewers feel as if they are playing a visual game'이 직접 설명
❌ ① 직접 그리는 것이 아니라 뒤집어 보는 것
❌ ② 디지털 변환은 16세기 맥락에 맞지 않음
❌ ④ 전문가만이 아니라 모든 관객이 즐길 수 있음
det.tip: interactive = 상호작용적. 관객이 그림을 뒤집는 행위 자체가 '상호작용'.

questions.passage: This witty and amusing creation is actually a work of art created by the visual artist Helga Stentzel. Using everyday items, she creates playful visual illusions that force you to look twice in order to confirm what you have just seen. Her unique style has been called "household surrealism." questions.stem: 밑줄 친 She가 가리키는 대상으로 적절한 것은?

det.korean: She = Helga Stentzel.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 문맥상 Stentzel이 영감을 얻은 이야기
❌ ② Arcimboldo는 남성
❌ ③ Rudolf II는 그림 속 인물
❌ ④ horse는 작품
det.tip: She = 여성 대명사 → 앞 문맥의 Stentzel.

questions.passage: Fruits, flowers, and vegetables are arranged like the pieces of a puzzle to create a human head. A cherry and a mulberry become the dark eyes, while an apple and a peach act as the pink cheeks. Each of Arcimboldo's works is a careful study of everyday objects. When he looked at typical objects, such as a bowl of vegetables, he saw the artistic and imaginative potential in <u>them</u>. His innovative approach to art inspired many great artists who came after him.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 대상으로 적절한 것은?

det.korean: them = typical objects(일반적인 사물). 그는 일반적인 사물 안에서 잠재력을 보았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② typical objects: 'looked at typical objects' → 'potential in them'
❌ ① great artists는 뒤에 나옴
❌ ③ composite portraits는 다른 맥락
❌ ④ 도구는 언급 없음
det.tip: them → 바로 앞의 복수 명사 typical objects를 가리킴.

questions.passage: You may think it is a quality that only artists and writers possess — some special talent you are either born with or without. Many people accept the idea that we can be divided into two groups: those who are creative and those who are not. This common belief, however, is far from the truth. Everyone has the ability to be creative.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"창의력은 예술가나 작가만이 가진 특별한 재능이라는 일반적 통념은 사실과 __________ 멀다."

det.korean: 이 통념은 사실과 거리가 멀다(far from).
det.analysis: ✅ far from: 'This common belief is far from the truth'에서 찾을 수 있음
